title: Arequipa guild march opposing quarantine and calling for work
location: Arequipa historic center; Plaza de Armas reached; exact route and venue-level boundaries unknown
scope: One local report documents an executed march by citizens associated with several guilds. The physical event date, exact route, relationship to other Arequipa reports, and start/end boundaries remain unresolved.
participants_original: Arequipa Misti Press describes “hundreds of citizens”; no counting method or bounded estimate is provided.
threshold_50_evidence: PER202102-S002 qualitatively describes hundreds of citizens marching. This clearly reports a crowd above 50, but supplies no count method, bounded number, or independent corroboration; do not convert it to a numeric minimum or borrow the unreviewed S001 headline.

title.summary: The opened report describes a guild-associated march through central Arequipa against the quarantine and for work; other Arequipa reports may concern a separate or related action.

start_date.summary: The body gives no physical march date. The 13 February 2021 article publication date is recorded on the source card but is not treated as event onset.

location.summary: The report places marchers in Arequipa historic-center streets and says they arrived at Plaza de Armas; exact route and boundaries are not described.

demands.summary: Signs opposed government quarantine and favored work/employment; named representatives also asked President Sagasti to meet worker and productive-sector groups and urged alternative COVID measures.

participants.summary: The report says “hundreds of citizens” but provides no method, bounded estimate, or merchant-only figure.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported qualitative crowd clearly exceeds 50, but cannot support a numeric minimum and has no independent corroboration.

end_date.summary: Arrival at Plaza de Armas is reported; the physical end or departure is not.

protester_violence.summary: The limited article text reviewed does not describe protester violence; code remains unknown rather than inferred absent.

state_response.summary: The report says municipal Serenazgo barriers were placed around the square to prevent movement against the scheduled measure; it does not establish an effect on this march or other response dimensions.

notes: Body evidence confirms that a public march was reported and supports a qualitative crowd above the 50-person threshold. Its exact physical date is absent, so February onset and unit ownership remain unresolved; do not use the 13 February publication date as the event date. The S001 “more than 500 merchants” headline is unverified and not used for this candidate. Written origin, outlet independence, and relation to E002 remain unknown. The preventive Serenazgo barriers are reported, but no effect or dispersal is inferred.
open_questions: On what physical date did the march occur, and did it begin in February 2021?
What was the basis for “hundreds,” and is there an independent or official turnout estimate?
Is S001 a separate account of this march, the same story/event, or another action?
Is this march distinct from the Arequipa reports grouped in E002?
What exact route, physical end, and effects, if any, followed the preventive barriers?
